tool.excerpt: Germany’s far-right AfD projected to win eastern state but unclear if it will be able to govern | CNN CNN 9/6/2026 Germany’s far-right AfD projected to win eastern state but unclear if it will be able to govern By Reuters Updated: 6:20 PM EDT, Sun September 6, 2026 Source: Reuters ‌The Alternative for Germany party surged into first place in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday, exit polls showed, putting a far-right party on the cusp of power at state level for the first time since World War II. With 44% of the vote, the AfD handed a drubbing to Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s conservatives, reflecting the deep unpopularity of Germany’s ruling coalition and the rise of hardline parties in a fracturing political landscape. If the AfD can translate its win into a majority of seats in the state parliament, it will secure a foothold for advancing its agenda at national level to heavily restrict immigration, restore ties with Russia, cut support to Ukraine and quit the euro. As counting continued, it remained unclear whether the AfD had secured enough votes to form a government but the wider political significance of the election, which according to broadcaster ZDF drew a turnout of 77%, was clear. “We have made history in this country,” said Ulrich Siegmund, the 35-year-old AfD lead candidate in Saxony-Anhalt, who drew thousands to his campaign rallies and who repeatedly cast victory in the state as a first step toward securing national power in federal elections due in 2029. As the first exit polls were published, he stood arm-in-arm with his party’s two national leaders, who laughed gleefully as the extent of the victory became clear. Jubilant celebrations broke out at the party’s election night gathering in the city of Magdeburg, where people waved German flags and hugged each other in triumph. Siegmund told CNN the election result will give his party the mandate to return to “sensible diplomacy” with both Russia and the United States. “We need both if we as Germany want to be successful,” he said.
